Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\mathrm{Stab}_{\rho}(\vee_n) \to 1, \qquad \mathrm{MaxInf}(\vee_n) = 2^{1-n} \to 0\)
    witness: \(\mathrm{OR}_n\)
    Perfect noise stability with no influential coordinate at all -- being nearly constant is enough.

No bound $\mathrm{Stab}_\rho = O(\mathrm{MaxInf}^k)$ exists. $\vee_n$ is asymptotically constant, so its variance vanishes and $\mathrm{Stab}_\rho(\vee_n) \to 1$, while every coordinate has influence only $2^{1-n}$. A function can be perfectly noise stable with no influential coordinate whatsoever -- it just has to be nearly constant.

see also: \(\mathrm{Stab}_{\rho}(f)\), \(\mathrm{MaxInf}(f)\), \(\mathrm{OR}_n\) data/relations/12-normalized.yaml

total No bound exists #

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\mathrm{Stab}_{\rho}(\vee_n) \to 1, \qquad \mathrm{NS}_{\delta}(\vee_n) = 2^{1-n}\big(1-(1-\delta)^n\big) \to 0\)
    witness: \(\mathrm{OR}_n\) ODonnell14
    OR is asymptotically constant, so it is perfectly noise stable and has vanishing noise sensitivity at the same time. The ratio $\mathrm{Stab}/\mathrm{NS}^k$ diverges for every $k$.

The same affine identity as in the other direction, $\mathrm{Stab}_{\rho} = 1 - 2\,\mathrm{NS}_{(1-\rho)/2}$, and the same reason it is invisible to a multiplicative matrix: no bound $\mathrm{Stab}_\rho = O(\mathrm{NS}_\delta^k)$ holds for any $k$.

see also: \(\mathrm{Stab}_{\rho}(f)\), \(\mathrm{NS}_{\delta}(f)\), \(\mathrm{OR}_n\) data/relations/12-normalized.yaml
